canonicalFacts.statement: Data/Item/ItemDrop.txt is a real file present in Blood Moon's actual server distribution.
Blood Moon's real ItemDrop.txt header row has 4 separate DropRate columns named DropRate_AL0, DropRate_AL1, DropRate_AL2, DropRate_AL3 (one per account/VIP tier), not a single DropRate column.

All 92 data lines in Blood Moon's real ItemDrop.txt are commented out (prefixed //), and every DropRate_AL0..AL3 value shown is 0 -- the per-item VIP drop-rate table is entirely inert/unused on Blood Moon.
The ProjectGamers/eMuGS vendor engine added 4 VIP-tier DropRate columns to ItemDrop.txt (replacing a single DropRate column) in an update the vendor labeled 7.0.
Custom Bot Store is a static NPC that sells a fixed list of items for zen and/or Cash, configured via Data/Custom/ text files.
Custom Bot Trader exchanges one player item for a fixed, pre-configured reward item, gated by a configurable success-rate percentage; on failure the input item is lost with no refund.
Custom Bot Trader supports a maximum of 30 bot instances of that type per server.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (comment present) / CONFIRMED_VENDOR_VIDEO (30 is the actual enforced max, not just documented)

canonicalFacts.statement: Custom Bot Fusion transfers Luck/Skill/Excellent-option rolls from a source item to a target item, at a configurable success rate; on success the source item loses its transferred options.

Custom Bot Fusion's real config field is named OnlySameType (not 'BotIndexOnly' as this sweep's initial transcript-based normalization guessed) -- when 1, restricts fusion to items of the same equipment category (e.g. sword-with-sword only); when 0, any category may be mixed. A separate DestinyLower flag additionally restricts fusion to cases where the destination item's level is within +/-10 of the source item's level.

The vendor's GameMaster.txt file has a Section 1 (in addition to the existing GM-commands Section 0) that whitelists specific account logins, by account level, for access to a specific Game Server instance.

Blood Moon's real Data/Custom/CustomBotBuffer.txt has its entire bot-placement table (section 1) commented out -- zero active buffer-bot entries, even though the cost/item-requirement/skill sections (2-4) below it are fully configured with 6 class-specific buffer templates (SM/BK/ELF/DL/SUM/RF).

Of the 4 vendor static-NPC bot systems present on Blood Moon (Store, Trader, Fusion, Buffer), only CustomBotStore is currently deployed active (1 live NPC, 'Luffen', a cash shop in Lorencia). Trader, Fusion, and Buffer all exist as configured files but have zero active/enabled entries.

Update 6.8 extends the EventItemBag end-of-event drop mechanism (already used by Blood Castle and Illusion Temple) to Devil Square, adding 7 configurable sub-indices (one per Devil Square level/stage).

Update 6.9 adds 'Reward Level' and 'Reward Points' columns to CustomMonster.txt, letting a specific monster grant direct character levels or a custom points currency on kill, in addition to the pre-existing Quest/GoblinPoint/Reset/MasterReset reward columns.
Pressing H shows a panel of currently-active event schedules, gated by a CustomEventTimer=1 flag in Data/Custom -- only enabled events appear in the list.
Custom Event PvP All is a GM-opened, player-joined kill-all PvP event where participants cannot attack each other until the GM closes/starts the event.
Custom Event PvP All scores kills at +2 points and deaths at -1 point by default, both independently configurable (death penalty can be set to 0).

Custom Event PvP All grants independently configurable currency rewards for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place finishers, drawn from multiple possible currencies (a ranking/honor-specific currency, WCoin, Gold, GoblinPoint).

Across every vendor-provided Data/Custom system independently verified against Blood Moon's real config so far (ItemDrop.txt, CustomBotTrader.txt, CustomBotFusion.txt, CustomBotBuffer.txt, CustomMonster.txt), the file is present with the correct/current column structure but every configured data row is commented out or Enabled=0 -- only CustomBotStore.txt (CLAIM-006/017) is an exception, with 1 genuinely active entry.

The vendor's engine (update 2.0.1.6) supports a ResetMin/ResetMax entry requirement for Blood Castle, Chaos Castle, Devil Square, and Illusion Temple -- a character's reset count must fall within the configured range to join, checked at join time (not just displayed); a value of -1/-1 disables the check.

Blood Moon's real Data/EventItemBagManager.txt (150 lines) is a flat index mapping 148 reward-bag entries to ItemIndex/ItemLevel/MonsterClass/SpecialValue/DropMap criteria, each referencing an individually-named file in a separate Data/EventItemBag/ folder (also 148 files, indices 000-147).

All 7 custom monster indices in Data/Custom/CustomMonster.txt (275, 361, 459, 561, 295, 801, 802) can be identified by name via cross-reference with EventItemBagManager.txt's MonsterClass column: Kundun, Nightmare, Selupan, Medusa, Erohim, Boss Farao, and Boss BloodMoon respectively.

Data/EventItemBag/147 - Boss BloodMoon.txt (MonsterClass 802) is a byte-identical copy of Data/EventItemBag/146 - Boss Farao.txt (MonsterClass 801), including an internal EventName field that still reads "Boss Farao" and an empty item-reward section (zero items configured to drop from either boss).

Blood Moon's real Data/Custom/CustomEventZombie.txt configures a daily 02:45 event (10-minute duration) with 4 monster waves (indices 14, 15, 55, 515) on Map 1, a 100%-rate cure-item drop (Type 14, Index 8) at the same coordinates as wave 3's spawn point, a Cash/Gold/PcPoint reward, and an entry NPC (class 380) on Map 0.

Blood Moon's real Data/Custom/CustomEventPandora.txt configures a daily 20:00 'Pandora Event' on Map 40 for 2-20 players of any class, where players' skins change to MonsterClass 55 (Skeleton King), in a bounded area, rewarding 100 Cash.

Blood Moon's real Data/Custom/CustomEventStopOrDie.txt configures a red-light/green-light style event on Map 1 with a 60s lobby, 30s countdown, randomized 4-8 second move windows, a 900ms stop-grace period, and a 500/500/500 Cash/Gold/PcPoint reward, entered via an NPC (class 684) at Map 1 coordinates (22,41).

4 entries in EventItemBagManager.txt (indices 102-105, Shining/Elegant/Steel/Old Jewelry Case) are commented out with a leading //, disabling them at the index-table level, even though their corresponding individual Data/EventItemBag/102-105 *.txt files still exist on disk.

Update 7.1 added a DropMap column to EventItemBagManager.txt, letting an admin restrict which specific map an EventItemBag reward is allowed to drop on, to avoid item clutter on unrelated maps (e.g. an Arena kill dropping the same reward as a specific field-boss kill).

canonicalFacts.statement: CustomAuctionEvent (ADDED 8.6) is a bid-based auction system activated via a Data/Command 'action' command (for free and/or VIP accounts) plus a Data/Custom config file, structured across 4 sections: event schedule, event name/alarm-time/duration, the auctioned item's full definition (index/level/durability/skill/option/socket/duration), and the currency/item required to place a bid.

CustomAuctionEvent's bid-currency field (Coin Type) supports at least zen(0) and item(4) as bid currencies, and when set to item(4) a separate config row defines exactly which item (by index/quantity) a player must hold to place any bid at all.

CustomAuctionEvent enforces that each new bid must be strictly greater than the current highest bid (a bid equal to or below the current highest is rejected with an in-game message); when the countdown ends, the highest bidder receives the auctioned item dropped on the ground at their location, and non-winning bidders keep their un-spent items/currency.

CustomEventRacer (ADDED 8.6) is a race event requiring 3 separately-configured NPCs (an entry/registration NPC, a finish-line NPC that awards the prize to the first player to click it after the race starts, and a waiting-area NPC), on top of the standard schedule/name/duration settings shared by other custom events.

CustomEventRacer supports both item-based and currency-based (Cash/Gold/PcPoint/WCoin/GoblinPoint) prize configuration via independent enable toggles, cross-referencing a named EventItemBag entry (demonstrated using index 145, labeled 'Event Racer') when item-reward is enabled.

The vendor (ProjectGamers) built the CustomEventRacer demo's standalone dungeon race-track map on client commission and offers the same map file free to any tutorial viewer who requests it directly; the same custom map is reused as the battle arena for the separately-covered Kill vs Kill event (see CLAIM-047).

CustomEventKillVsKill (ADDED 8.5) is an automated single-elimination 1v1 tournament event with a configurable 'Max Score' (best-of-N deaths before elimination), a minimum player-count, and a level range gate; the vendor explicitly warns against setting the minimum level to 1 because the game engine's own minimum attack-eligible level is 6.

CustomEventKillVsKill supports 4 distinct reward-type modes selected by a single RewardType field (1=character attributes, 2=EventItemBag items, 3=currency, 4=VIP time), and can be scheduled per-class (one weekday/time slot per character class, plus a separate 'all classes' slot) or opened on demand via a GM command independent of any schedule.

Using a non-town (custom/dungeon) map as CustomEventKillVsKill's battle arena additionally requires configuring a matching entry in a separate Data/Custom respawn-gate manager file plus the death-warp gate table, otherwise a player who dies inside the event's battle map is teleported to Lorencia by the engine's default death-warp rule and cannot return to the event.

A GM-only panel (opened with the D key, visible only to accounts holding GameMaster.txt permission) provides one-click buttons to open nearly every custom event this sweep has catalogued: 10 town Arenas (index 0-9), Team vs Team, Russian Roulette, Absorption, Hide and Seek, Drop Event/Drop Npc, BBB, Battle Royale, Racer, the core castle-family events (Blood Castle/Devil Square/Illusion Temple/Chaos Castle), Invasion Manager (indices 0-27), Capture the Flag, a Guild-vs-Guild-adjacent option, a generic PvP-event option, and a raffle ('sorteio') option -- each button simply invokes the corresponding existing GM command rather than adding new event logic.

A separate player-facing panel (also opened with the D key, a 'Join Event' tab) lets any player join whichever event a GM currently has open without typing the /join command, and is enabled/visible via its own independent config flag, distinct from the GM panel's flag.

Update 8.1 adds a monster-model hover-preview (the cursor icon changes to show the tied monster's in-game appearance) plus a 2-field freeform text hint (e.g. a drop-chance callout like '20% chance to drop Bless/Soul') to each entry in the H-key event-schedule panel, both configured per-event in Data/Custom/CustomEventTime.txt.

CustomMapRequirement (ADDED 8.0) lets an admin require players to hold specific item(s) and/or a currency amount (Cash/Gold/PcPoint/WCoin/GoblinPoint) before they can move to a configured map by /move command or the in-game map-teleport UI; on a successful move, the required item(s) and currency are automatically deducted from the player.

In CustomMapRequirement, setting an item's fields to an asterisk (*) disables that item's requirement check entirely (currency-only enforcement), and independently setting all currency amounts to 0 disables the currency requirement (item-only enforcement) -- the two requirement types are independently toggleable, and leaving both empty/zero disables the feature for that map entirely.

CustomGuildVsGuild (rewritten UPDATED 6.9) is a throne-capture event: a 'crown' NPC spawns automatically at event start (and despawns at event end) at a configured map/coordinate; a guild member clicks it to claim the throne, and rival guild members must kill the current holder and click the NPC themselves to steal it. The winning guild (by total hold time/score) receives a guild-wide reward, and a separate top-5 individual ranking receives its own reward.

CustomGuildVsGuild requires a minimum guild-member count (admin-configured) to be eligible to participate, and -- new in update 6.9 -- supports a 'zone block' (map + coordinate rectangle) that physically prevents players from crossing into the event area until the event officially starts, automatically unlocking at the configured start time.

Configuring CustomGuildVsGuild's entry NPC requires adding matching map/coordinate entries in 3 separate places that must all agree: the CustomGuildVsGuild config file itself, the monster/NPC placement file (MonsterSetBase.txt), and a separate NPC-type command-routing config (referred to in the video as 'NPC Viaturas' / Custom NPC) -- a mismatch in any one breaks the NPC's function.

Update 6.6 adds 2 new event entries to the H-key event-schedule panel (index 4=Crywolf, index 5=a Castle-Siege-affiliated event) plus a new 'monster quantity' column applying to invasion-type entries; the Castle-Siege entry only appears in the panel when the viewing player is connected to the GameServerCS instance (or standing on the Crywolf map), because those 2 events are specific to that separate server instance rather than the main GameServer.

The H-key event panel only lists events/invasions that are currently enabled -- a disabled entry (demonstrated live: Custom Arena, turned off) is silently omitted from the list entirely rather than shown greyed-out, meaning panel absence is not reliable evidence a feature doesn't exist -- it may simply be off, or (for Castle-Siege/Crywolf specifically) the viewer may not be connected to the right server instance.

The /join (participar) player command only works for a whitelisted subset of events; it explicitly does NOT work for CustomArena, Battle Royale, or DropNpc, which instead require the player to click a dedicated map NPC to enter.

The /openevent (Abrir evento) GM command's syntax depends on whether the target event supports multiple configured instances: multi-instance events (e.g. CustomArena, 10 slots indexed 0-9) require both an index number and a name string that must exactly match the event's registered command string; single-instance events (e.g. Roleta Russa) always use index 0 with just the name string.

CustomGuildMapMove (ADDED 6.3) lets an admin designate a specific map as exclusive to one named guild (e.g. as an event-victory reward) -- only members of that exact guild (not even allied guilds) can move to the map; anyone else's move attempt is rejected with an in-game message naming the map's current owning guild. Multiple maps can each be independently assigned to different guilds simultaneously.

The original 5.7 version of the H-key event panel is built from 2 separate config sections: an 'Invasion Manager' list (the engine's fixed original events plus up to 5 free custom slots at indices 9-13, whose names are looked up from the language/Messenger file by message-ID) and a separate 'Custom Arena' list (its own 0-9 index range); the available Custom Arena slot count varies by base engine season (fewer slots on Season 2/3 and pre-Season client 97d than on Season 4+).

Any edit to the H-key event panel's config requires regenerating the client-side .mpg file (via GetMyInfo) and copying it into the client folder before the changes take visible effect in-game -- the same GetMyInfo -> mpg -> client-copy workflow this sweep has observed for several other GetMyInfo-driven features (e.g. CLAIM-060/061).

CustomCaptureTheFlag (ADDED 5.4) awards a point to a team in exactly 2 ways: (a) a member returns the enemy team's stolen flag to their own team's designated NPC, or (b) a member kills an enemy player who is currently carrying their team's own stolen flag (which simultaneously returns the flag and scores the point) -- killing a non-flag-carrying opponent never scores a point.

In CustomCaptureTheFlag, dying while carrying the enemy's stolen flag causes the flag to be dropped/returned to its origin point, requiring another player to steal it again; team assignment (Red/Blue) on event entry is fully automatic/random with no player choice, and a tied score at the event's time limit results in no declared winner.

CustomEventRobber (ADDED 4.7) spawns a monster that steals either just the randomly-targeted victim's inventory items, or their entire loadout (equipped gear + inventory + wings + pet), per 2 independently toggleable config scopes; only the targeted victim can damage this specific monster instance, and killing it returns 100% of the stolen items plus some bonus loot the monster itself drops.

If CustomEventRobber's targeted victim disconnects before recovering their items, the monster despawns and the stolen items are automatically returned to the player -- an explicit no-item-loss guarantee even on disconnect.

CustomEventOnClick ('Evento Veloz'/quick-click) spawns a single NPC at a scheduled time; the first player to click it wins a combination of item (via a linked EventItemBag entry), currency, and/or VIP time, and subsequent clicks by other players after the prize is claimed yield nothing, with the winner's name broadcast server-wide.

CustomEventOnClick's VIP-time reward is configured independently for free vs. already-VIP players (distinct tier and day-count fields for each), specifically so a player who already holds a higher VIP tier isn't accidentally downgraded by winning a lower-tier VIP reward from the event.

GameServer/DATA/GameServerInfo - Custom.dat is a single master switchboard (758 lines) containing an on/off Switch flag for nearly every Data/Custom feature, serving as the authoritative real source for whether a given custom system is enabled on Blood Moon -- independent of whether that system's own Data/Custom/*.txt file has populated rows.

Blood Moon's real Data/Util/ResetTable.txt exists but contains zero configured data rows -- only its header comment (MinReset/MaxReset/Level_AL0-3/Money_AL0-3/Point_AL0-3 columns) and an "end" marker.

Blood Moon's real /reset command (GameServerInfo - Command.dat) is ENABLED and requires exactly level 400 to use, on all 4 VIP tiers; grants 1 reset per use, 450 stat points on tier AL0 or 500 on tiers AL1-3, resets the character to level 1, and enforces no item/money/quest/skill cost; the total-reset cap is 20 for tiers AL0-AL2 but 50 for tier AL3 (the highest VIP tier).

Blood Moon's real /masterreset command is DISABLED (CommandMasterResetSwitch=0) even though its full parameter set is configured as if ready to use: requires level 400 and 1000 prior resets, resets the character back to level 400 with 0 reset count, grants 0 stat points, with no per-tier variation in these requirements.

Data/Custom/CustomMonsterTime.txt provides real, direct MonsterClass-to-MapNumber associations for 5 monster instances (4 active, 1 commented): MonsterClass 412 on Map 42 (commented "Dark Elf 3° Quest Refuge"), MonsterClass 275 (Kundun) on Map 36, MonsterClass 801 (Boss Farao) on Map 8, MonsterClass 295 (Erohim) on Map 31 (commented "Erohim Land of Trials"), and MonsterClass 802 (Boss BloodMoon) on Map 33 -- 2 additional rows (Nightmare on Map 39, Selupan on Map 58) are commented out/inactive.

Blood Moon runs a "Custom Market Shop" (player-to-player listing system) that is ENABLED (CustomMarketShopSwitch=1) with a 5% transaction tax and no per-account item cap -- this feature is not described in any project-gamers-oficial video processed by this sweep.

Blood Moon has a "Custom Pix" payment-integration feature (CustomPixSwitch) present in config but DISABLED, with its URL field still set to the vendor's own unconfigured placeholder value ("https://seudominio.com.br/pix.php") and all 6 price-package fields at 0 -- indicating it was never set up, not merely turned off after use.

Blood Moon's real Data/EventItemBagManager.txt index 32 currently reads MonsterClass 275 with the comment "//Kundun" -- confirming CLAIM-029's original finding and CONTRADICTING the "Condor" name given in video b5S00cPpUBg (CLAIM-037). No evidence was found of index 32 ever having held a different MonsterClass value.

Blood Moon's GameServerInfo - Command.dat contains a "Command Buy Vip Settings" block for the native in-game /buyvip <tipo> <dias> command, with three VIP slots (Vip1-3) that each carry three currency price values (PriceValue1-3).

canonicalFacts.statement: On the code in this repository branch, crediting a paid recharge (RechargeIntent to a WC_PURCHASE_CREDIT ledger row via WalletLedgerService, currently through the Mercado Pago provider; the Asaas provider lives on other worktrees and was not audited) writes only the Portal's own ledger: the payments, wallet and commerce modules contain no reference to GameBridgeJob, CashShopData or MU_DATABASE_URL, so no automatic bridge from Portal WC into game currency exists in this code.

In the preserved legacy Free MU CMS (DmN) PHP source, a confirmed web donation credits game currency through reward_user() then add_credits() then increase_credits(), a config-driven UPDATE of <table>.<column> = <column> + :credits whose target comes from admin config keys (credits_<server>|table_<type>, |credits_column_<type>, |account_column_<type>); the documented target for the game currencies is CashShopData (WCoinC, WCoinP, GoblinPoint).
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC_CODE_READ (preserved legacy source; the code path is read, the exact type-to-column config values were not -- GAP-P18-03)

canonicalFacts.statement: Currency-slot numbering is not uniform across Blood Moon's subsystems: CustomEventAuction.txt CoinType is 1-3 with 0 = zen; CustomCoinsOnline.txt carries CoinType rows 0, 1 and 2 with no legend in the file (inferred 0-based); X-Shop prices are Coin0/Coin1/Coin2; the vendor Lua API uses Coin1/Coin2/Coin3 -- so a raw slot number must never be carried from one subsystem to another.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (the numbering as written in the files) / INFERENCE (that CustomCoinsOnline.txt is 0-based -- no legend, GAP-P20-06) (preserved snapshot, read 2026-09-18; not re-read live)

canonicalFacts.statement: The word "GameBridge" names at least six distinct things in this repository -- GAME_COMMAND_TRANSPORT (HMAC to Worker/D1/Queue to Agent to SQL procedure), MARKETPLACE_DELIVERY_WORKER (an always-failing script), PORTAL_BRIDGE_JOB_OUTBOX (the shared GameBridgeJob table), GAME_DATA_TELEMETRY (read-only game-to-cloud ingest and heartbeat), GM_EVENT_EXECUTOR_STUB and a label-only future data dependency -- and a seventh in the vendor Lua "bridge functions" (engine event hooks); the Agent process hosts both GAME_COMMAND_TRANSPORT and GAME_DATA_TELEMETRY.

GameBridgeJob is a shared Portal-side outbox used by three features (marketplace escrow, VIP delivery via GRANT_VIP, account lifecycle via ANONYMIZE/PURGE), and the marketplace script process-game-bridge-jobs.mjs selects every PENDING job regardless of operation, so with MU_BRIDGE_ENABLED=true it would mark jobs owned by the other dispatchers PROCESSING and then FAILED.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC_CODE_READ (the selection query was read; the "would fail them" consequence follows from the read code, the flag has never been set true)

canonicalFacts.statement: The committed Worker (apps/game-data-worker/src/commands.ts, identical blob on all 43 branch refs (39 local + 4 remote-tracking)) accepts only CREATE_GAME_ACCOUNT and its D1 schema.sql still has CHECK (command_type = 'CREATE_GAME_ACCOUNT'); the Portal client types, the Agent handlers and the D1 migration 0004 exist for GRANT_VIP, SYNC_VIP_TIER, ANONYMIZE_GAME_ACCOUNT and PURGE_GAME_ACCOUNT, but the Worker routing for them exists only as uncommitted changes in the mu-bloodmoon-v1-openbeta worktree -- so those four commands cannot flow end to end from committed code.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC_CODE_READ + git blob comparison (2026-09-18); the openbeta working tree may change

canonicalFacts.statement: As of the preserved Phase 3D-A evidence (2026-08-24), the production command transport was deployed and active for CREATE_GAME_ACCOUNT only: the Worker, Queue and D1 (migration 0003) existed, the VPS task BloodMoonGameBridgeAgent was running, one real QA account was created with exactly the two authorised MU rows, and a response-loss / Agent-restart / lease-expiry replay wrote nothing twice; the production writer login's only permission is EXECUTE on dbo.DmN_CreateGameAccount; the four extension commands were not deployed and several later runbooks nevertheless say the Agent was never deployed.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (preserved 2026-08-24 evidence, read 2026-09-18; current state NOT re-verified -- GAP-P20-02)

canonicalFacts.statement: No currency-credit command exists in the command transport, and none of its idempotency layers is sufficient for an additive credit: the Worker, claim lease and Agent SQLite ledger are keyed by transport ids, the existing procedures are repeatable by nature (MAX rule, state checks, credential-hash replay), the SQL audit table's CommandId index is non-unique and no procedure consults it, and after a crash between a SQL commit and the ledger completion the ledger re-acquires the command after 30 seconds and calls the writer again.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC_CODE_READ; the crash-window behaviour is read from code and was not executed (no test of that window was found in the Agent test files searched)

canonicalFacts.statement: The only acknowledgement the command transport can give is that the stored procedure returned and committed: the Agent talks only to SQL Server, has no channel to the GameServer process, writes succeed whether the GameServer is online or offline, and the Worker/D1 result carries a status and result code, not proof that the game sees the change.

In the lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup, dbo.WZ_SetCoin(@Account, @Name, @Value1, @Value2, @Value3) ADDS each positive value to CashShopData (WCoinC = WCoinC + @Value1, WCoinP = WCoinP + @Value2, GoblinPoint = GoblinPoint + @Value3), ignores zero and negative values so it cannot subtract, inserts a row holding only that column when the account has none (the other columns take their default 0), uses no BEGIN TRAN (XACT_ABORT is ON but each statement autocommits and the three blocks are not atomic together), takes no lock (IF EXISTS then INSERT is racy: a concurrent first credit fails on the primary key), never uses @Name, and has no idempotency key, ledger, audit or return code, so calling it twice credits twice.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: In the lab restore, dbo.CashShopData is (AccountID varchar(10) NOT NULL with collation Latin1_General_CI_AS, WCoinC int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, WCoinP int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, GoblinPoint int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) with a clustered primary key PK_TempCashShop on AccountID as its only index, and no CHECK constraint, no foreign key in either direction and no trigger, so negative balances are representable and rows can exist for accounts that are absent from MEMB_INFO.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: Every stored procedure in the restored GameServer database that changes CashShopData balances is additive (col = col + value) -- WZ_SetCoin, WZ_SetExchangeReward, WZ_SetKD, WZ_CustomMonsterReward, WZ_SetRewardCastleSiege and WZ_SetRankingDay/Mon/Wek -- while three ranking procedures only run the no-op UPDATE GoblinPoint = GoblinPoint; no procedure sets an absolute balance, none subtracts (no debit procedure exists), and only WZ_SetCoin inserts a missing row: the others silently credit nothing to an account that has no row.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: The vendor procedures label the same three balances Cash | WCoinC, Gold | WCoinP and PcPoints | GoblinPoint and keep commented Season 4 alternatives that write MEMB_INFO.Cash, MEMB_INFO.Gold and PcPointData.PcPoint instead of CashShopData.WCoinC, WCoinP and GoblinPoint (WZ_SetCoin, WZ_SetExchangeReward, WZ_SetKD for Cash and Gold, WZ_SetRewardCastleSiege, WZ_SetRankingDay/Mon/Wek), confirming first-hand that Cash/Gold/PcPoint are the Season 4 names of the balances that Season 6/8 store as WCoinC/WCoinP/GoblinPoint, slot for slot.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: The vendor procedure WZ_SetRewardCastleSiege selects the guild members to reward through MEMB_STAT.ConnectStat = 1 (players who are online) and credits them WCoinC/WCoinP/GoblinPoint by a plain additive SQL UPDATE on CashShopData; nothing in the database shows whether the GameServer keeps its own in-memory copy of a balance.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: In the lab restore, dbo.CustomPlayToEarn(Account varchar(10) NOT NULL, WCoinC int, WCoinP int, GoblinPoint int, each NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, clustered primary key PK_CustomPlayToEarn on Account) is a second table holding the same three balances; it has 0 rows and is referenced by no stored procedure, view or trigger, so its role is unknown.
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_RUNTIME (lab restore of the 2026-07-16 production backup; the procedure/table was NOT re-read on production and nothing was executed)

canonicalFacts.statement: The Agent kill switches are AgentOptions.GrantVipEnabled, SyncVipTierEnabled, AnonymizeEnabled and PurgeEnabled (all default false), bound from the Agent configuration section, which Program.cs also reads from environment variables carrying the prefix BLOODMOON_AGENT_ (for example BLOODMOON_AGENT_Agent__GrantVipEnabled); the names GAME_BRIDGE_GRANT_VIP_ENABLED and its siblings that the documents use appear only in comments and documents; no code or script reads an environment variable of that name (the tracked template deploy/game-bridge/Start-GameBridgeAgent.ps1 sets BLOODMOON_AGENT_Agent__* variables but none of the four switches).
canonicalFacts.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC_CODE_READ (the standard .NET double-underscore section separator; not exercised)

explicitlyNotCanonical_contradicted.statement: The vendor's own ItemDrop.htm tutorial document (as normalized in docs/vendor-tutorials-knowledge-extraction.md) lists ItemDrop.txt's fields as a single 'DropRate' column, not 4 VIP-tier columns.

The reworked CustomMonster/CustomNPC system (ADDED 7.2) supports 5 distinct client-side 'Type' visual modes for a custom entity: 0=NPC using a stock NPC-folder BMD model, 1=Monster using a stock Monster-folder BMD model, 2='Golden Monster' variant, 3=NPC assembled entirely from a 7-slot equippable item-set instead of a dedicated BMD model file, 4=Monster assembled the same equipment-set way.

The item-set-based NPC/Monster appearance (Type 3/4, see CLAIM-066) uses a fixed 8-slot layout (0=Helm, 1=Armor, 2=Pants, 3=Gloves, 4=Boots, 5=Weapon1, 6=Weapon2/Shield, 7=Wings), each slot independently able to reference any real in-game item index/category and independently settable to Excellent quality; as of this video there is no Pet slot in this system, explicitly noted by the vendor as a possible future addition, not yet built.

A custom NPC configured with a shop (via a Shop Manager index plus a matching individual shop file) will fail to open its shop in-game unless the map number and X/Y coordinates in the shop config exactly match the coordinates configured for that same NPC in the monster/NPC placement file (MonsterSetBase.txt).

CustomEventRobber supports 2 relevant targeting configurations: a general random-victim pool restricted to characters meeting a minimum Reset/Master-Reset/status-stat threshold (each independently disabled via -1), or a 'PK-only' mode that restricts the random-victim pool to currently PK-flagged players standing in open-PvP areas, excluding anyone inside a safe town.
